Subject: Threshold key split + network boundary runthrough for Acme private deploy

Team — looping everyone in for a focused runthrough of the HSM and BYOK plan for Acme's private deployment next week. Acme has strict requirements: operator separation, no key material leaving customer HSMs, and a documented emergency rotation path.

High-level asks:
- Mina: can you attach the current operator runbook and confirm the proposed split (2-of-3) threshold scheme fits our runtime?
- Priya / SecureVault: would like your recommended HSM network layout (management plane vs data plane) and attestations for import.
- Vivek: need exec thumb on any deviations from standard BYOK import for Acme (they require dual-operator approval + offline unwrapping).

I attached a rough segmentation diagram and the draft runbook; please review and add inline comments. Goal is to finalize before the dry-run on 3/16.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Product Manager, Private Deploy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hsm-segmentation-draft.pdf, operator-runbook-v0.9.md

Cc: Priya Rao <security@securevault.com>, David Jenkins <david.jenkins@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Threshold key split + network boundary runthrough for Acme private deploy

Jonas — thanks. Quick notes after first pass of the runbook:

- Confirmed approach: 2-of-3 threshold with one share kept in customer HSM, one share in Redwood HSM (dedicated tenant slot), and one share sealed in an external escrow (encrypted blob stored in customer S3). This preserves customer custody while allowing recovery.
- Operator separation: We propose two distinct operator roles: HSM-Admin (export/import controls) and Network-Admin (firewall/VPC peering). Both require MFA + YubiKey.
- Rotation cadence: recommend quarterly scheduled rotations + an emergency rotation play that kicks off if a share is suspected compromised. Emergency rotation requires an authenticated call to Redwood's control plane and manual operator presence from Acme.
- Networking: will enforce management-plane-only access to HSM nodes from a dedicated bastion in the customer's VPC; data-plane inference traffic never traverses that management path.

Attached: operator-runbook-v0.9.md (redline comments inline). I added an escalation matrix and a checklist for the dry-run.

-Mina
Mina Haddad
Manager, Private Deploy Ops
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Threshold key split + network boundary runthrough for Acme private deploy

Thanks for the details, Jonas / Mina. A few clarifications from SecureVault:

1) Import path: for BYOK we recommend an offline import token flow (customer generates key locally, wraps with HSM import key, then performs split-shares inside the HSM) — this avoids exporting cleartext ephemeral keys. We'll supply the attestation artifacts for the import key.

2) Network segmentation: agree with management-plane bastion. Additionally we suggest:
   - On-host HSM firewall allowing only Redwood's signed management API calls (mutual TLS)
   - Time-bound ephemeral management credentials minted per session (we can integrate with the customer's STS)

3) Operator model: SecureVault supports an HSM operator service that enforces a hardware-backed approval (attested operator token). If you want, we can do a demo of the operator approval flow during the dry-run.

I'll attach a short configuration checklist and our suggested firewall rules (pdf). Let us know what day/time for a 30m test.

-Priya
Priya Rao
Principal Security Engineer, SecureVault Solutions
security@securevault.com

Subject: Fwd: Threshold key split + network boundary runthrough for Acme private deploy

Forwarding SecureVault's notes — Vivek, one decision item for you: Acme requires offline unwrapping and dual operator approval during import. This deviates from our usual streamlined import and will add ~2 hours to the dry-run and a small ops overhead (ephemeral credential orchestration + offline token handling).

If you approve, I'll lock the dry-run and schedule SecureVault for a 30m demo plus the import dry-run on 3/16. If you prefer we keep the standard import flow, we'll need to get Acme to relax the offline requirement.

-Jonas

1) Add an emergency rotation play into the runbook that can be executed without SecureVault if network connectivity to their HSM management plane is lost. (High-level steps only — we can refine after the dry-run.)
2) Ensure we capture the billing implications of the more manual import flow for the deal team (I don't want surprise credits).

Once those are addressed, lock the 3/16 dry-run and confirm attendees.
